What if you ran
as fast as you
possibly could, and still
moved backward?
Now, connect the dots
and face the terrifying
conclusion of this
mathematics.
If the speed of
expansion increases steadily
with distance, there must
inevitably come a critical
threshold where the
expansion rate exceeds
the speed of light itself.
And that threshold is real.
At a distance of
approximately 14.5 billion
light-years from Earth,
space is stretching away
from us faster than
186,000 miles per second.
Astronomers call this
boundary the Hubble sphere.
You might immediately ask:
does this violate Einstein's
sacred rule that nothing
can move faster than light?
The mind-bending answer is no.
Special relativity dictates
that no physical matter
or signal can move
through space faster than
light.
However, it places no
speed limit on space itself!
Space has no mass,
no physical friction,
and no inertia.
Spacetime can stretch faster
than light without breaking
a single law of physics.
Imagine you are running
on a giant mechanical
treadmill.
Your top running speed
is 10 miles per hour.
But the treadmill surface
beneath your feet is
accelerating backward at
20 miles per hour,
then 50, then 100
miles per hour.
No matter how fiercely
you pump your legs,
no matter how much
fuel you burn,
you will not only
fail to move forward—you
will be dragged backward
into the darkness.
This is a simple
picture of what happens
to a starship,
or even a beam
of light, trying to
reach the most distant
galaxies.
The cosmic treadmill moves
faster than your maximum
speed.
This catastrophic boundary
leads to the Cosmic
Event Horizon.
Much like the event
horizon surrounding a black
hole from which no
light can ever escape,
the cosmic event horizon
is a boundary of
causal separation.
It sits roughly 16
billion light-years from
us today.
Any galaxy beyond it
is permanently and
irrevocably severed from us.
Even if you fired
a beam of light
right now toward those
regions, that light would
travel forever and never
bridge the gap,
because the intervening
space is expanding too fast.
That boundary is not a wall.
It is a line
where cause and effect
can no longer connect.
The full video shows
what pushes it closer
every day.
